title: paretosecurity: 0.0.89 -> 0.0.91, nixos/paretosecurity: add trayIcon option
reason: Applicable: real paretosecurity module + wired test. Real diff is the ORIGINAL introduction of trayIcon (a new mkEnableOption, plus a new lib.mkIf cfg.trayIcon {} systemd unit) -- the PR that the later batch2 restructurings (393366/397890) build on top of.
targets_toml: single target paretosecurity, cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,paretosecurity], watch=[trayIcon].

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: 3rd instance of the wastebin-class candidate_capability_gap (tally: wastebin/B3, this one). check-head.json's discovered_options is COMPLETELY EMPTY for this file (same total-non-discovery shape as wastebin, not just the watched option) -- confirmed the cause is the SAME dotted-path declaration idiom: paretosecurity.nix declares `options.services.paretosecurity = { enable = ...; package = ...; trayIcon = ...; };` (dotted-path form), matching wastebin's own `options.services.wastebin = {...}` exactly. This is now 3 modules sharing this exact idiom and this exact total-non-discovery symptom -- strong, repeated evidence this is a real, systematic gap.
